answer: Based on the NOAA wildfire dataset, controlling for weather conditions (wind speed, relative humidity, energy release component, and rainfall), more aggressive suppression (full suppression strategy) is associated with significantly shorter fire duration (coefficient = −0.95, p < 0.001), meaning fires do end faster; however, it is also associated with significantly more buildings affected (coefficient = +1.79, p < 0.001), meaning aggressive suppression does NOT reduce building impacts — in fact, fires receiving full suppression tend to affect more buildings, likely because full suppression is disproportionately deployed on larger, more threatening fires near populated areas
